title: How to start training a neglected body part
summary: NH explains that a neglected muscle builds a tonnage debt that must be repaid with both effort and time, not aggressive volume. He recommends building frequency first, then volume, being careful with tendons, and accepting that the part will likely never become a strong point.
claims: Novice programs tend to neglect small body parts, so most lifters must play catch-up later
Muscle grows chronologically: two years of neglected calves cannot be made up in two months
Aggressive volume and intensity cannot make up lost time; it only burns you out
The neglect is a debt repaid with both effort and time; neither alone works
Everyone wants bigger calves but nobody trains them because calf raises are boring; that is why most have small calves, him included
You cannot have bad genetics for a body part you never train
If a body part does not grow from compounds you must isolate it; those who grow from compounds alone, e.g. triceps from close-grip bench, are anomalies
Do not neglect another body part while catching up; that replaces a bad thing with a worse one
Commonly neglected parts are small muscles like calves, rear delts, traps and forearms, which need special attention beyond compounds
Integrate the neglected part slowly, focusing on frequency first: start once a week, then 2, then 3 times, before increasing volume and sets
Every two days is a good frequency; even small muscles need recovery
Neglected muscles come with neglected tendons; a torn Achilles recovers poorly even with surgery, so do not start calves heavy
The muscle should always give up before the tendon; feeling tendons, knee pain after squats or low back pain after deadlifts means poor technique or poor volume/intensity control
Overuse injuries come from training tendons more than muscles
Having a body is a privilege and a duty; neglecting a part is mistreatment that must be paid back gradually
The neglected part will most likely never catch up or become a strong point, because other parts keep accumulating tonnage; it will still grow
Most people complaining about a small body part cycle between hype, overtraining, burnout, blaming genetics and renewed motivation
exercises: start low frequency, light, build up
